Shri Sunil Kumar Dubey, learned counsel for the applica  Shri Saket Udhaniya, learned Public Prosecutor for the   ORDER This second application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 83/2023 registered at Police Station Pathari, District Vidisha (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 342, 376(2)(n) and 376(3) of the IPC and Section 3& 4 of the POCSO Act.
Applicant is in judicial custody since 13/05/2023.
First bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 07/09/2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 33993/2023.
Thereafter, victim (P.W.1), her mother (P.W.2) and brother (P.W.3) have been examined before the Trial Court.
As per the case of prosecution, brother of the victim, reported to PS Pathari, District Vidisha that his younger sister, aged 15 years, is missing since evening of 25/04/2023.
He suspects that unknown offender has enticed and taken her sister.
On such allegations, PS Pathari registered FIR at Crime No. 83/2023 for offence punishable under Section 363 of the IPC against unknown person.
Victim was 2 MCRC-16037-2024 recovered from Jaipur.
Victim stated that Rahul Ahirwar (applicant) had taken her to Bhopal and Jaipur.
They were staying in a rented room at Jagatpura, Jaipur.
Rahul had promised to marry her and committed assault assault on her.
Police has brought her back to PS Pathari.

On such allegations, prosecution for offence punishable under Sections 366, 342, 376(2)(n)
and 376(3) of the IPC and Section 3& 4 of the POCSO Act was added.
Relevant seizures were made.
Applicant was arrested on 13/05/2023, he is in custody ever since.

On completion of investigation,
Final Report was submitted.
Trial is underway.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant has falsely been implicated in this matter under pressure of family members of the victim.
Victim had left her parental home at her own and came to stay with him because they are close relatives.
Learned counsel referring to statements of victim (P.W.1), her mother (P.W.2) and brother (P.W.3) submits that victim and her family members did not support the prosecution.
Victim has made no allegation against the applicant in her evidence before the Trial Court.
Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that material witnesses have been examined.
There is no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence by the applicant.
Applicant is aged 26 years.
He is labourer by profession.
He is already married.
He has family to look after.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family and home.
No criminal antecedent is reported against him.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra , learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Learned counsel referring to DNA report submits that DNA report implicates the applicant.
In reply, learned counsel for the applicant submits that no male STR DNA profile was found from person of the victim.
DNA was matched with undergarments of the victim which creates doubt on veracity of the DNA profile.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
